# Agent integration compatibility

<!-- Generated from config/agent-integrations.json; do not edit by hand. -->

Support describes this repository integration, not every upstream product capability.
**native** uses the target's own mechanism; **alternative** uses an implemented adapter or an
explicit script; **unsupported** has no repository equivalent for that feature.

In Claude Code and OpenCode use `/plan`, `/implement`, `/lightweight`, `/inbox`, or
`/dispatch`. In Codex CLI use `$iw-plan`, `$iw-implement`, `$iw-lightweight`,
`$iw-inbox`, or `$iw-dispatch` followed by the same inputs, or select through `/skills`.
Codex skills require explicit invocation. Dispatch starts workers only when requested.
Orca is a session host, not a worker execution backend. Reuse the hosted backend's
existing commands or generated skills; no separate Orca workflow commands are needed.
Repository workers select their session host independently of their execution backend;
Orca launch, continuation and guarded cleanup preserve repository approval gates.
See [local setup](../../setup/local.md#orca-workspaces).

An execution backend runs the agent; a session host launches, displays and manages
its sessions. Each compatibility target below declares its role.

- **claude-instructions**: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory

- **opencode-permissions**: https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/

- **repository-tests**: scripts/tests/test_worker.py and scripts/tests/test_worktree_prune.py; CLI/API mocks, not live sessions. Installed audit versions: Claude Code 2.1.322, Codex CLI 0.167.1, OpenCode v2.2.5.
- **codex-sandbox**: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing
- **codex-app-server**: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server
- **claude-agent-view**: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view
- **opencode-sdk**: https://opencode.ai/docs/build/sdk
- **worker-live-visibility**: Local smoke evidence on 2026-11-11: Codex native task was listed by the current TUI and executed pwd/branch checks in its assigned worktree; OpenCode created, read, listed, and deleted a sibling-worktree session without a model turn. Claude native listing shape checked against the installed CLI; new launch validation uses mocked regression tests.
- **worktree-local-configuration**: Repository fixture tests cover explicit and Claude-hook creation, sibling-master source selection, current/future backend resource paths, preserved destinations, shared edits, ignore checks, private output, failure retention and source preservation on removal. No backend API or CLI contract changes.
- **orca-api**: Orca 1.4.261: bundled CLI and orchestration guides, recovery reference and installed command schemas. Worker launch, mutation replay IDs, same-chat follow-up assignment transfer, guarded release and non-forced workspace removal validated locally. orca.yaml parsed with the installed setup resolver.
- **development-setup-tests**: scripts/tests/test_dev_setup.py and test_worktree_prune.py: setup preflight/failure propagation and WORKTREE-007 existing-checkout linking. Runtime setup starts no services; Gradle frontend development-server arguments checked separately.
- **orca-worker-tests**: scripts/tests/test_orca_worker.py: ORCAWORKER-001 through ORCAWORKER-008 contract fixtures. Disposable live Codex structured-chat smoke verified workspace identity, same-conversation continuation, approval-phase cleanup refusal and release/workspace/branch removal. Terminal and other backend combinations use contract tests, not a claim of live parity. Project-selection regression fixtures cover duplicate checkout registrations, hidden projects, archived workspaces, explicit selection and continuation after a project is hidden.
- **handoff-tests**: scripts/tests/test_handoff.py: approval/context integrity, ownership, direct developer question routing, transport-specific replay, retirement and acceptance fixtures; no live workers launched or stopped.
- **orca-developer-launch**: Installed Orca CLI agent launch, terminal show/send/close and chat command schemas and bundled guides reviewed 2026-11-23; installed adapter implementation confirms launch operationId/retry-launch, journaled or handed-to-terminal prompt receipts, worktree inventory identity and ptyKilled close proof. Chat CLI offers rename only; continuation manual and automatic chat retirement unsupported. Contract fixtures are not live session evidence.

## Maintenance

Follow [ADR-0014](../adr/0014-cover-agent-integrations-across-backends-and-hosts.md).
Edit the compatibility manifest and canonical Claude commands/settings, then run
`python3 scripts/sync-agent-config.py`. Do not edit generated skills, this matrix, or
`opencode.json`. The same script with `--check` runs through documentation checks in CI.
The generator-owned file list is `.agents/generated-skills.json`; regeneration removes
obsolete owned files only when their previous content is intact, preserving other skills.

When changing agent CLI/API code, hooks, or permissions, review every affected target
and update the reviewed input hashes and affected review dates in the manifest. Revalidate
official sources when upgrading a backend or host. Dates record evidence review, not an expiry or
a guarantee that CI detects upstream changes. Record newly introduced configuration files
and mechanisms in the same change; review is still needed for integrations outside the
known directories and worker operations. Local Claude settings are developer-owned and
are excluded. Generated `iw-*` skill paths are reserved for the generator.

AGENTS.md approval gates are process instructions. They do not enforce a shell permission
boundary. Codex retains its configured sandbox/approval policy; Claude shell wildcards
are not converted into Codex execution prefixes. No repository Codex permission adapter
or native worktree-hook adapter is installed. In Codex and OpenCode create and remove
worktrees through `scripts/worktree.sh`, including for workers; native worktree lifecycle
operations bypass this repository's layout and cleanup checks.

Worker launch/resume/delete adapters are covered by mocked CLI/API regression tests.
The recorded versions are audit context, not a claim that live backend sessions were
launched or deleted during verification. Keep lifecycle requirements in
[Protocol parallel](../protocols/parallel.md).
